beats.narration_text: Ciao — this is Liam, in for Komal. Luxury talks circular like a campaign color. The real problem is identity: you cannot recirculate a bag you cannot prove is real. Watch how A.I. and digital product passports turn secondhand from a trust problem into a market.

props.command: How can AI help luxury close a circular economy — name the identity bottleneck, one real authentication case, and the Digital Product Passport fix.
output: Bottleneck: you cannot recirculate what you cannot prove is real
Case: Vestiaire — experts scaled by machine learning
Fix: Digital Product Passport — the object carries its record

beats.narration_text: Here's the whole idea. A circular luxury economy keeps the object in use — resale, repair, reuse — instead of landfill. That only scales if the object stays legible: authentic, priced, findable. A.I. does the identity work. The passport is the record. Sustainability is what you get when the second sale still works.

show.event: Card: keep the object in use

beats.narration_text: The old luxury chain is a straight line: design, cut, sell, forget. Circularity bends that line into a loop. Houses love the loop on a slide. They hate the operational question: who proves this jacket is real, and who captures the second sale?

Here's the bottleneck. A used bag without a receipt is a rumor. Counterfeits poison the resale price of the real thing. Human authenticators cannot inspect every listing. So the loop stalls at trust. Until the object can identify itself, circular is a donation bin with better lighting.

Vestiaire Collective is the worked example. Over one hundred fifty experts across five hubs, plus machine learning in the verification stack. In twenty twenty-four, roughly ten percent of listings failed digital checks — images, condition, and fakes in the same filter. A.I. multiplies the expert. It does not replace the expert.

beats.narration_text: Europe is adding the record: a Digital Product Passport under Ecodesign. Materials, origin, care, end-of-life — reached from a data carrier on the product. Textiles are a priority. The Commission plans the textile act in late twenty twenty-seven, not an overnight twenty twenty-six switch. Bain and eBay: a passport can double lifetime value. About ninety percent of brands still see red tape.

beats.narration_text: Here's the design tell. Theater prints a green lookbook and parks a take-back bin. Mechanism authenticates, passports the object, and lets it re-enter the market. If second-life volume does not rise, the circular story is marketing. Full stop.

Let's recap with Claude. Circularity in luxury is an identity problem. The loop needs authentication plus a product record. Vestiaire shows the hybrid: experts scaled by A.I. Europe's passport is the compliance flywheel — textile rules still being written, planned late twenty twenty-seven. Bain: most brands still see a burden. Design judgment: if used goods cannot be trusted, they cannot circulate.

Record: EU Digital Product Passport (ESPR) — textiles are a priority; delegated act planned Q4 2027.
Economics: Bain/eBay — a passport can double lifetime value; ~90% of brands still see a burden.
The rule: if second-life volume does not rise, the circular story is marketing.
